bull_bear.body:
- No debt; does not plan to raise debt. Preferential allotment in-principle approval received; funds expected imminently.
- Cash ~INR 20 cr (as of 31-Dec-2025).
- Disciplined: cut low-visibility miniature-bellows outlay, redeploy to demand-backed projects (liquid cooling, hoses, annealing).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- US tariff (50%) — biggest market (US ~55% of exports); blocks new-customer onboarding; bellows ramp delayed.
- Heavy export concentration (74% sales; EU+US ~85% of exports) and single-customer dependence in liquid cooling (5-yr exclusive, India-only).
- Liquid-cooling demand entirely partner-forecast-driven; data-center capex cyclicality.
- Execution: capacity additions across hoses/assemblies/bellows running behind schedule.
- SS raw-material price volatility (partially hedged).
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: Confident but measured ("Q3 good, not very good"); candid on Q1 weakness, bellows being behind schedule, and tariff drag on new customers. Emphasis on long-term margin path and moat narrative.
bull_bear.title: Mgmt tone

bull_bear.body:
- Liquid-cooling skid is flow-control IP adaptable beyond data centers (large machinery, semiconductor, HVAC, EV cooling) — collapse-of-DC optionality.
- Partner intends to make the India entity a **global supply hub** for skid assemblies in 3–4 years (exports possible ~6 months out) — large latent upside beyond the India-only INR 350 cr peak.
- Moat = 15–20 yrs flow-control engineering + proprietary flow-simulation software + customer access, not just "changing a hose design."
- Assembly growth is self-reinforcing: more assemblies → more captive hose-braid production.
- India–EU FTA structurally neutralizes Turkish duty-free advantage in EU.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious

bull_bear.body:
- Global technology partnership with a US-based data-centre infrastructure leader providing early entry and commercial traction in liquid cooling
- Established global customer relationships and export presence across 90+ countries diversified across Americas, Europe and Asia
- Deep innovation pipeline: 58 products under R&D across various stages, including 16 specifically for data-centre liquid cooling
- Engineering differentiation, product quality and customer intimacy cited as basis for competing against new entrants
- Investment in automation and robotic welding lines strengthening throughput and product quality
- Vertical integration and end-to-end fluid-flow capability via Hyd-Air Engineering acquisition, with German technology-enabled capabilities
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Export and geopolitical concentration — Geopolitical tensions, trade restrictions, tariff measures, sanctions and regional economic disruptions may affect demand, pricing and supply-chain continuity across the Company's 90+ export markets; the ongoing Middle East conflict and residual trade-policy uncertainty add to global fragmentation risk.
- Foreign exchange risk — Currency fluctuations may affect export realisations, profitability and the value of foreign-currency-denominated transactions, given the Company's significant international revenue exposure.
- New product / liquid-cooling adoption risk — In the thermal-management business, the pace of liquid-cooling adoption in Indian data centres remains at an early stage relative to North America and Europe; longer customer qualification cycles, higher initial investment costs for operators and the prevalence of gas-based cooling in India's installed base may moderate the near-term revenue ramp.
- Market and demand risk — Slowdowns in industrial activity, changes in customer spending patterns, competitive intensity and sector-specific demand fluctuations may impact order inflows, capacity utilisation and revenue growth.
- Supply chain risk — Disruptions in raw material availability, logistics bottlenecks or supplier concentration may affect production schedules and customer deliveries.
- Regulatory and compliance risk — Changes in environmental regulations, export controls, trade policies, taxation frameworks and industry-specific standards across domestic and international markets may increase compliance costs or affect market access.
- Operational risk — Manufacturing interruptions arising from equipment failures, process inefficiencies, utility disruptions or human error may impact productivity, quality and customer commitments.
- Technology and cybersecurity risk — Increasing reliance on digital systems exposes the Company to risks related to cyberattacks, data breaches and system failures.

outlook.body: Aeroflex pursued capacity expansion on multiple fronts during FY26 and into FY27. SS flexible hose capacity was augmented by 1.0 million metres in Q3FY26 to 17.5 million metres p.a. installed as at 31 March 2026 (~70% utilisation during the year), with a further expansion to 20 million metres p.a. on track for completion by Q2FY27. In the assemblies business, two robotic welding lines were added in Q4FY26 (46 assembly stations as at 31 March 2026), and the Company plans to add more assembly stations together with commissioning an automatic welding station and annealing plant by December 2026. The new SFN liquid-cooling skid assembly line was scaled from 2,000 units p.a. installed capacity in December 2025 to 6,000 units p.a. as at 31 March 2026, with further expansion to 9,000 units targeted in Q2FY27 en route to a total installed capacity of 15,000 units p.a. by Q2FY27. Hyd-Air Engineering (wholly owned subsidiary) upgraded its quality laboratory and R&D centre at Chakan, Pune. The Company also derives benefits from a 750 KW rooftop solar power project installed at its Taloja manufacturing facility (installed in the previous financial year) and operates a NABL-accredited Research & Development Laboratory; during FY26 it incurred R&D expenditure of ₹395.50 lakhs focused on new product development, including liquid-cooling solutions for data centres and AI infrastructure.

outlook.body:
- India's sustained industrial capex cycle (National Infrastructure Pipeline, PM Gati Shakti, PLI schemes) is expanding addressable demand across oil & gas, petrochemicals, refineries, power generation, ports and terminals, and firefighting systems
- Make in India initiative and defence indigenisation (IDDM framework) are opening new addressable markets in aerospace and defence for certified Indian manufacturers
- Structural shift toward liquid cooling in data-centre and AI infrastructure is the most significant medium/long-term opportunity; global liquid-cooling market expected to grow nearly tenfold by 2034 and India's nearly fourteen-fold over the same period
- Energy transition and clean-energy infrastructure (green hydrogen, solar) expanding application of flow-control products in high-purity gas handling and thermal management
- India's emerging semiconductor fabrication and electronics manufacturing base creating demand for ultra-precision vacuum/wafer-handling products
- Rapid EV adoption creating demand for bellows in battery thermal management and cooling
- Diversified end-market presence and strong customer stickiness helping sustain growth momentum despite headwinds in certain export markets
- Domestic market witnessed particularly strong growth driven by project demand across ports, irrigation, oil & gas, petrochemicals and steel sectors
- Increasing adoption of value-added products (assemblies, bellows, liquid-cooling solutions) expected to further strengthen business mix and enhance profitability
- Pace of liquid-cooling adoption in Indian data centres (early-stage relative to North America/Europe) flagged as principal risk moderating near-term revenue ramp for the thermal-management business
- Competitive intensity in both core and new businesses is a continuous risk addressed through engineering differentiation, product quality and customer intimacy
- Aeroflex enters FY27 with a strong outlook, supported by a healthy order pipeline, established customer relationships and a strong balance sheet
- Continuous orders and dispatches under the long-term agreement with the US-based data-centre infrastructure partner reflect the strength of the Company's engineering capabilities and R&D expertise

- Liquid-cooling peak revenue INR 300–350 cr, peak utilization ~FY29 (2–2.5 yrs); near-term dispatch pipeline INR 45 cr.
- Metal bellows: current run-rate INR 12 cr → INR 36 cr in next few quarters; peak ~INR 85 cr by end-FY28/start-FY29 (behind schedule due to US tariff delays).
- Hyd-Air: INR 45 cr peak at current capacity (capex to expand coming soon).
- Aggregate peak revenue potential >INR 1,000 cr over next ~3 years.

growth_optionality.title: Growth
growth_optionality.body:
- Quarterly exports +30% YoY (EU major contributor) despite tariffs; 9M export growth still single-digit due to very weak Q1.
- EU framed as next strong leg — India–EU FTA expected to boost competitiveness vs Turkey (duty-free EU access); EU was flat ~3 years.
- Domestic up strongly 9M — new ports/terminals & chemical customers, deeper wallet share in steel.
- Liquid-cooling TAM: global ~$3bn now, ~33% CAGR → ~$21bn over 6–7 yrs.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's sustained industrial capex cycle (National Infrastructure Pipeline, PM Gati Shakti, PLI schemes) is expanding addressable demand across oil & gas, petrochemicals, refineries, power generation, ports and terminals, and firefighting systems
- Make in India initiative and defence indigenisation (IDDM framework) are opening new addressable markets in aerospace and defence for certified Indian manufacturers
- Structural shift toward liquid cooling in data-centre and AI infrastructure is the most significant medium/long-term opportunity; global liquid-cooling market expected to grow nearly tenfold by 2034 and India's nearly fourteen-fold over the same period
- Energy transition and clean-energy infrastructure (green hydrogen, solar) expanding application of flow-control products in high-purity gas handling and thermal management
- India's emerging semiconductor fabrication and electronics manufacturing base creating demand for ultra-precision vacuum/wafer-handling products
- Rapid EV adoption creating demand for bellows in battery thermal management and cooling
- Diversified end-market presence and strong customer stickiness helping sustain growth momentum despite headwinds in certain export markets
- Domestic market witnessed particularly strong growth driven by project demand across ports, irrigation, oil & gas, petrochemicals and steel sectors
- Increasing adoption of value-added products (assemblies, bellows, liquid-cooling solutions) expected to further strengthen business mix and enhance profitability
- Pace of liquid-cooling adoption in Indian data centres (early-stage relative to North America/Europe) flagged as principal risk moderating near-term revenue ramp for the thermal-management business
- Competitive intensity in both core and new businesses is a continuous risk addressed through engineering differentiation, product quality and customer intimacy
- Aeroflex enters FY27 with a strong outlook, supported by a healthy order pipeline, established customer relationships and a strong balance sheet
- Continuous orders and dispatches under the long-term agreement with the US-based data-centre infrastructure partner reflect the strength of the Company's engineering capabilities and R&D expertise

margins.title: Margins
margins.body:
- Q3 EBITDA margin 23.5–23.6%, mix-led (value-added 54%). Took 8% price discount on US tariff but protected bottom line via internal cost optimization + vendor cost-sharing.
- Liquid-cooling margins undisclosed (single-customer confidentiality) but > hoses, ~= assemblies.
- RM (SS wire/coil) managed via back-to-back planning + long-term supplier contracts; prices broadly stable last couple of years.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- No debt; does not plan to raise debt. Preferential allotment in-principle approval received; funds expected imminently.
- Cash ~INR 20 cr (as of 31-Dec-2025).
- Disciplined: cut low-visibility miniature-bellows outlay, redeploy to demand-backed projects (liquid cooling, hoses, annealing).

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Aeroflex pursued capacity expansion on multiple fronts during FY26 and into FY27. SS flexible hose capacity was augmented by 1.0 million metres in Q3FY26 to 17.5 million metres p.a. installed as at 31 March 2026 (~70% utilisation during the year), with a further expansion to 20 million metres p.a. on track for completion by Q2FY27. In the assemblies business, two robotic welding lines were added in Q4FY26 (46 assembly stations as at 31 March 2026), and the Company plans to add more assembly stations together with commissioning an automatic welding station and annealing plant by December 2026. The new SFN liquid-cooling skid assembly line was scaled from 2,000 units p.a. installed capacity in December 2025 to 6,000 units p.a. as at 31 March 2026, with further expansion to 9,000 units targeted in Q2FY27 en route to a total installed capacity of 15,000 units p.a. by Q2FY27. Hyd-Air Engineering (wholly owned subsidiary) upgraded its quality laboratory and R&D centre at Chakan, Pune. The Company also derives benefits from a 750 KW rooftop solar power project installed at its Taloja manufacturing facility (installed in the previous financial year) and operates a NABL-accredited Research & Development Laboratory; during FY26 it incurred R&D expenditure of ₹395.50 lakhs focused on new product development, including liquid-cooling solutions for data centres and AI infrastructure.

management_tone.title: Mgmt tone
management_tone.body: Confident but measured ("Q3 good, not very good"); candid on Q1 weakness, bellows being behind schedule, and tariff drag on new customers. Emphasis on long-term margin path and moat narrative.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Global technology partnership with a US-based data-centre infrastructure leader providing early entry and commercial traction in liquid cooling
- Established global customer relationships and export presence across 90+ countries diversified across Americas, Europe and Asia
- Deep innovation pipeline: 58 products under R&D across various stages, including 16 specifically for data-centre liquid cooling
- Engineering differentiation, product quality and customer intimacy cited as basis for competing against new entrants
- Investment in automation and robotic welding lines strengthening throughput and product quality
- Vertical integration and end-to-end fluid-flow capability via Hyd-Air Engineering acquisition, with German technology-enabled capabilities

risks.title: Risks
risks.body:
- US tariff (50%) — biggest market (US ~55% of exports); blocks new-customer onboarding; bellows ramp delayed.
- Heavy export concentration (74% sales; EU+US ~85% of exports) and single-customer dependence in liquid cooling (5-yr exclusive, India-only).
- Liquid-cooling demand entirely partner-forecast-driven; data-center capex cyclicality.
- Execution: capacity additions across hoses/assemblies/bellows running behind schedule.
- SS raw-material price volatility (partially hedged).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious
non_obvious.body:
- Liquid-cooling skid is flow-control IP adaptable beyond data centers (large machinery, semiconductor, HVAC, EV cooling) — collapse-of-DC optionality.
- Partner intends to make the India entity a **global supply hub** for skid assemblies in 3–4 years (exports possible ~6 months out) — large latent upside beyond the India-only INR 350 cr peak.
- Moat = 15–20 yrs flow-control engineering + proprietary flow-simulation software + customer access, not just "changing a hose design."
- Assembly growth is self-reinforcing: more assemblies → more captive hose-braid production.
- India–EU FTA structurally neutralizes Turkish duty-free advantage in EU.
